officialDocsConsulted.summary: Bun.spawnSync accepts cwd and a stdin option typed Writable (TypedArray, Blob, Response, BunFile, fd) and returns SyncSubprocess with Buffer stdout/stderr, numeric exitCode and a success boolean; unlike Bun.spawn there is no stdin property on the result, so a payload must be passed through the stdin OPTION rather than written incrementally. findings.text: The new missing-criteria arm of buildNotPlannableReason is unreachable by the test suite, so US-001 AC4 is verified by nothing but a substring grep. Reviewer checks: (a) grep -rn 'no acceptanceCriteria in spec' test/ returns zero hits, so no test asserts the emitted string; (b) buildNotPlannableReason is only called from resolveSpecificIssue (plan.ts:155) when !isPlannable, and every specified/open fixture that reaches runPlan now carries a default spec (makePlannable at test/plan.test.ts:106 and the readBacklogFn inline entries at test/attach-hint.test.ts:141/166 all gained spec.acceptanceCriteria in this diff); the three deliberate negative fixtures at test/plan.test.ts:350-402 override status/stage/blockedBy only and never empty the criteria. The branch therefore cannot be entered by any test. The AC4 oracle `grep -q 'acceptanceCriteria' src/commands/plan.ts` would stay green if the branch were deleted and replaced by a comment, or if it were reordered after the isBlocked check (which would silently make cam plan report 'blocked by an unshipped dependency' for a criteria-less blocked issue instead of the real cause). This is the tautological-oracle shape the project's own patterns.md warns about ('deliver the FORM of the oracle, not the claim'). Mechanical fix, one file: add a runPlan test with a specified/open/unblocked entry whose spec.acceptanceCriteria is empty, asserting exit 1 and that the printed reason names the missing-criteria case (note test/plan.test.ts sits at its new 629 ceiling, so the same commit will need another justified file-size raise).

The real-CLI refusal path exercises only the missing-spec shape under --derived-from. US-002 AC6 is worded 'a missing or invalid spec', and the guardrail is claimed to apply uniformly to both flags. The invalid shapes (empty acceptanceCriteria array, blank scope) and the --fast-track flag are covered at the unit layer (test/issue-file.test.ts:857-925), so the behavior is tested, but the end-to-end exit-code plus machine-line contract is only proven for one of the four combinations. Consider one extra real-CLI case with --fast-track and an empty acceptanceCriteria array.

validateSpec only checks that acceptanceCriteria is a non-empty array; it does not check that its entries are non-empty strings. A payload of spec.acceptanceCriteria = [""] (or [123]) passes the new filing guardrail and is persisted verbatim by buildIssueEntry, after which isPlannable's length-based check also passes. The gate that ADR-0051 exists to enforce can therefore be satisfied with a single empty-string criterion. Reusing validateSpec was explicitly mandated by the PRD and tightening it would also affect the cam spec interview path, so this is out of scope for this branch, but it is a real residual hole worth a follow-up: an entry-level isNonEmptyString check in validateSpec would close it without a bespoke re-implementation.

The bullet added this cycle contains an em dash ('do not eyeball the sentence for "does this convey the idea" - inline code-formatting a token...'). The global convention bans em dashes in persisted human-readable .md. The file already carries 38 on main so this is consistent with the file rather than a regression, and no gate enforces it; noting it only so the drift is deliberate rather than accidental.
